Rasagiline and Intranasal Epinephrine: Rasagiline enhances the effects of intranasal epinephrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Safinamide and Intranasal Epinephrine: Safinamide increases the effects of intranasal epinephrine via pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 3. Selegiline (Oral and Transdermal) and Intranasal Epinephrine: Both oral and transdermal forms of selegiline potentiate the effects of intranasal epinephrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Intranasal Epinephrine and Sodium Chloride (Intranasal): Intranasal epinephrine may increase the systemic absorption of sodium chloride due to alterations in the nasal mucosa, which can persist for up to two weeks post-administration. Monitor closely. 5. Intranasal Epinephrine and Sotalol: Sotalol can either increase or decrease the effects of intranasal epinephrine. Pharmacodynamic synergism may enhance effects, while antagonism may reduce them. Monitor carefully. 6. Intranasal Epinephrine and Spironolactone: Spironolactone may enhance the effects of intranasal epinephrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor for potential cardiac arrhythmias, especially if co-administered with cardiac glycosides, diuretics, or antiarrhythmic drugs. 7.
